1.note: See how you translated **under the sun** in 1:3. This also occurs in verse 12.

2.note: Qoheleth is not referring to a specific **person**. He means anyone in this situation in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Anyone to whom God gives]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **wealth**, **possessions**, and **honor**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [many valuable things that he owns and many people who honor him]
Here, **his soul** represents his appetite. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [for his appetite anything]

2.q: לֶ⁠אֱכֹ֣ל מִמֶּ֔⁠נּוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ נָכְרִ֖י יֹֽאכֲלֶ֑⁠נּוּ
2.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the wealth that God gives were food that a person could **eat**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to enjoy it; instead, a nonnative person will enjoy it]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if this situation were **vapor**, which appears for a moment and then is gone. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 9. Alternate translation: [this situation is fleeting and empty]

3.q: אִם־יוֹלִ֣יד אִ֣ישׁ מֵאָ֡ה וְ⁠שָׁנִים֩ רַבּ֨וֹת יִֽחְיֶ֜ה
3.note: Qoheleth is presenting a possible condition, that a man might father many children and live for many years. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [Perhaps a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years]

Qoheleth says **a hundred children** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [an extremely large number of children]

3.q: וְ⁠שָׁנִים֩ רַבּ֨וֹת יִֽחְיֶ֜ה וְ⁠רַ֣ב ׀ שֶׁ⁠יִּהְי֣וּ יְמֵֽי־שָׁנָ֗י⁠ו
3.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [and he should live an exceedingly great number of years]

The expression **his soul is not satisfied** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [but if he does not find satisfaction]

This could mean: (1) that this man does not receive an honorable burial, which was a great disgrace in this culture; Alternate translation: [he does not even receive an honorable burial] or (2) that he lives forever and so does not need to be buried. Alternate translation: [if he were to live forever]
If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [I say that the stillborn child is better than him]

4.note: Qoheleth is referring to being born and dying in a polite way by using the phrase **in vapor it came, and in the darkness it will go**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [it was conceived, and it died]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the child’s name were an object that **the darkness** hides from sight. He means that no one ever remembers this child. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and no one will ever remember its name]

The expression **its name will be covered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one will remember its name]

5.note: Qoheleth is using **Even the sun it did not see** as a common expression of the culture to mean “it never lived.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [It never lived]

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [nor did it know anything about life]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **rest**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [This one rests better]

The pronoun **this one** occurs twice here. The first instance refers to the stillborn child and the second instance refers to the man who has wealth but does not enjoy it. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [belongs to this stillborn child than to that man]

6.note: Qoheleth says **And if he lived a thousand years twice** to introduce an imaginary situation to help explain that even a very long life has no value if a person does not enjoy it. Use a natural method in your language for introducing an imaginary situation. Alternate translation: [And imagine a man who lived a thousand years twice]

Qoheleth says **a thousand years twice** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [an extremely long time]

Qoheleth is using **a good thing he did not see** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he did not enjoy his life.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but he did not enjoy his life]

Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that every person dies, no matter how long he lives. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [both of them certainly go to one place!]

Qoheleth is referring to dying in a polite way by using the phrase **going to one place**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [both going to die]

7.q: כָּל־עֲמַ֥ל הָ⁠אָדָ֖ם לְ⁠פִ֑י⁠הוּ וְ⁠גַם־הַ⁠נֶּ֖פֶשׁ לֹ֥א תִמָּלֵֽא
7.note: Qoheleth uses or invents a proverb in order to show that people work only to satisfy their appetites and yet are never satisfied. Translate this proverb in a way that will be recognized as a proverb and be meaningful in your language and culture. Alternate translation: [All people’s labor goes into their mouths, yet their appetite is never satisfied]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **toil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [All that humanity works for]

Here, **his mouth** represents the food that he eats. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [is for the food that he eats]

The expression **the soul is not filled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [nothing fills the soul]

Here, **the soul** represents the appetite, not the spirit. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the appetite is not satisfied]

8.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that a wise person has no lasting advantage over a foolish person. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For the wise person has no advantage over the fool!]

Qoheleth is using the adjective **the wise** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [belongs to a wise person more than to a foolish person]

Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that a poor person who knows how to conduct himself well gains no lasting advantage either. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [The poor person who knows how to walk before the living has no advantage either!]

Qoheleth is using **to walk before the living** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to conduct himself well among other people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to conduct himself well among other people]

Qoheleth is using the adjective **the living** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [before people who are alive]

9.note: Qoheleth uses or invents a proverb in order to teach that being content with what a person already has is better than craving what he does not have. Translate this proverb in a way that will be recognized as a proverb and be meaningful in your language and culture. Alternate translation: [Better to enjoy what the eyes already see than to crave what one does not have]

Qoheleth is using **a sight of {the} eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “what a person already has.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is what a person already sees before him]

Qoheleth is using **the walking of {the} soul** as a common expression of the culture to mean “desire that is never satisfied.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [than craving what one does not have]
See how you translated **pursuit of wind** in 1:14.

10.note: The expression **its name has been called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [already it has a name]

The expression **it is known** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people know what a person is]

The implication is that **he who is more powerful than him** is God. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [God, who is far more powerful than any person]

11.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that speaking many words brings no benefit to people. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [there is no advantage at all for humanity.]

12.q: כִּ֣י מִֽי־יוֹדֵעַ֩ מַה־טּ֨וֹב לָֽ⁠אָדָ֜ם בַּֽ⁠חַיִּ֗ים מִסְפַּ֛ר יְמֵי־חַיֵּ֥י הֶבְל֖⁠וֹ
12.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one knows what is good for a person to do during his brief life. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For no one knows what is good for humanity in life during the number of the days of his vaporous life.]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the shadow** is brief and quickly gone, so are the days of a person’s life. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And he makes the days of a person’s life brief and fleeting, quickly gone like a shadow]

The pronoun **he** refers to God, and the pronoun **them** refers to the days of a person’s life. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And God makes the days of a person’s life]

12.q: אֲשֶׁר֙ מִֽי־יַגִּ֣יד לָֽ⁠אָדָ֔ם מַה־יִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָ֖י⁠ו תַּ֥חַת הַ⁠שָּֽׁמֶשׁ
12.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one is able to tell a person what will happen after he dies. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For no one will declare to humanity what will be after him under the sun.]

Here, **what will be after him** could mean: (1) what will happen after he dies. Alternate translation: [what will happen after he dies] or (2) what will happen to him later in life. Alternate translation: [what will happen to him in the future]
